Deterministic work/node budgets improve reproducibility compared with wall-time cutoffs, provided model construction, solver version, seed, parameters and parallel mode are fixed. Gurobi guarantees repeatable WorkLimit stopping points on the same hardware/settings; IBM notes that deterministic parallel node limits can overshoot while workers synchronize. Report elapsed time separately: equal node counts need not mean equal computational effort. [Gurobi documentation](https://docs.gurobi.com/projects/optimizer/en/current/reference/parameters.html), [IBM documentation](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/icos/22.1.2?topic=optimizers-determinism-parallelism-optimization-limits).

Timeouts without a feasible incumbent remain unresolved, not proven infeasible. A direct accounting bound: with F certified feasible and U unresolved among N instances, eventual feasibility lies in [F/N, (F+U)/N], assuming all remaining instances are certified infeasible. This identification interval is distinct from a sampling confidence interval. Report feasibility found within budget, unresolved fraction, incumbent quality and optimality bounds separately. Runtime cutoffs create right-censored observations; dropping timeouts or substituting the cutoff as the actual runtime biases runtime estimates downward. Adaptive stopping may require additional censoring assumptions; a fixed administrative cutoff alone does not establish informative censoring. [Censored-runtime research](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/21279).

Repeated perturbations within users are dependent. Resample whole users, retaining their perturbations and paired method results, then recompute the comparison; stratify by category when estimating a category macro-average. These are design implications of cluster-bootstrap methods, which preserve within-subject dependence. More perturbations improve measurement within users but do not create additional independent users; confidence intervals remain fragile with few user clusters. [Cluster-bootstrap study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7148287/).
